headline: 34 platoons of BGB deployed in industrial areas of Dhaka, Gazipur, Narayanganj
summary: Border Guard Bangladesh forces are stationed in key manufacturing hubs to maintain order and prevent unrest.
details: Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has deployed 34 platoons of personnel to the industrial areas of Dhaka, Gazipur, and Narayanganj.
The deployment is aimed at maintaining law and order in these critical manufacturing hubs.
The forces are stationed to prevent any potential unrest or disruptions to industrial production.
This move comes as a measure to ensure stability in the regions where major factories and factories are located.

headline_marked: Sheikh Hasina [[requests new passport and NID]] to return to Bangladesh
headline: Sheikh Hasina requests new passport and NID to return to Bangladesh
summary: The ousted Prime Minister, currently in India, intends to return in December to surrender before a court following her death sentence for crimes against humanity.
details: Ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has requested a new passport and National Identity Card (NID) to facilitate her return to Bangladesh from India, according to a Reuters report.

In a letter sent by her London-based lawyers to the acting high commissioner in Delhi, Hasina requested the documents be processed expeditiously, noting that her previous documents had been revoked by the interim government.

Hasina informed Reuters that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December to surrender before a court. Her aides stated that the specific date will be announced once the necessary formalities are completed.

The move comes after she was sentenced to death in absentia by the International Crimes Tribunal in November last year for the deadly crackdown on student protesters in 2024, charges which she has denied.
Analysts suggest her return could either sharpen political divides and threaten stability in Dhaka or potentially ease the strained diplomatic ties between Bangladesh and India.
Currently, the Awami League is banned in Bangladesh, and many of its members remain jailed or in self-imposed exile.
caption:
Sheikh Hasina is seeking a new passport to return to Bangladesh and surrender to the court.

Ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has requested a new passport and National Identity Card (NID) to facilitate her return to Bangladesh from India, according to a Reuters report.

In a letter sent by her London-based lawyers to the acting high commissioner in Delhi, Hasina requested the documents be processed expeditiously, noting that her previous documents had been revoked by the interim government.

Hasina informed Reuters that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December to surrender before a court. Her aides stated that the specific date will be announced once the necessary formalities are completed.

The move comes after she was sentenced to death in absentia by the International Crimes Tribunal in November last year for the deadly crackdown on student protesters in 2024, charges which she has denied.

Analysts suggest her return could either sharpen political divides and threaten stability in Dhaka or potentially ease the strained diplomatic ties between Bangladesh and India.

Currently, the Awami League is banned in Bangladesh, and many of its members remain jailed or in self-imposed exile.
